# Recorded runtime stream fixtures

Captured once per case from the installed 2.1.286 CLI in the repository's
`test-vault`, using print/verbose/stream-json with partial messages, safe mode,
restricted tools, no MCP, and the adapter's permission rules. No fixture is
fabricated. Tests replay these files without calling a real model.

- `runtime-normal.jsonl`: "Say hello in one sentence", read-only, small model.
- `runtime-tool.jsonl`: initial edit-mode protected-folder check (two denied Writes).
- `runtime-tool-final.jsonl`: repeat against final Windows permission rules: three
  Writes attempted, two explicitly denied. The normal-folder overwrite was rejected
  by the tool's read-before-write prerequisite, **not** a permission denial; it does
  not demonstrate a successful allowed write.
- `runtime-error.jsonl`: nonexistent model selected for one short greeting. The
  recorded result has `is_error: true` even though its subtype is `success`.

Privacy redaction replaces the vault prefix with `<test-vault>`, other profile
paths with `<redacted-local-path>`, and UUIDs with a fixed UUID. Account/auth-source
metadata is omitted. Partial tool-input JSON is assembled, redacted, and repartitioned
so path fragments cannot leak a username and still parse to valid redacted JSON.
Tool/message IDs are opaque event identifiers, not account IDs. Stream structure,
text, costs, errors and usage are retained. Redaction is not evidence of runtime
output being generated by a fake adapter.

`total_cost_usd` is cumulative across CLI session resumes. Parser tests preserve
that raw value; adapter tests verify subtraction of `RunRequest.previousCostUsd`,
which Chat supplies from the persisted session total, including after reload.

## Hermes ACP (Step 10)

`hermes-acp-permissions.json` contains selected real server frames recorded through
Chat on 2026-10-16 with installed Hermes 0.21.5 and
`openrouter:cohere/north-mini-code:free`. It retains tool calls, per-edit requests,
streaming reply chunks and the final per-turn estimated cost ($0). The vault prefix
is replaced with `C:/Vault`; provider inventories, auth metadata, thoughts and
unhandled housekeeping notifications are omitted. This is a recorded permission
check, not generated model output. The replay test substitutes its own session/RPC
IDs and fragments the JSON bytes; no model or filesystem write is used.

The real run denied `AgentHQ/Agents/step10-denied.md` and wrote the allowed Work
file. Later final-build checks repeated denial/resume and a successful mixed-team
Work write; see `docs/evidence/step10-checks.json` for costs and the taskkill race
found/fixed during verification.

## OpenCode ACP (Step 11)

`opencode-acp-permissions.json` records 25 selected real server frames from
OpenCode CLI 1.19.1 with `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`: an allowed Work write,
a denied protected write, a denied out-of-scope read, and a resumed allowed read
with a streamed marker and native USD usage. Vault paths are replaced with
`C:/Vault` (both slash forms); thoughts, authentication and inventories are
omitted. Tool/RPC identifiers remain opaque protocol identifiers.

The ACP test replays these frames in 17-byte fragments with its own session ID,
uses the real OpenCode permission callback, and waits for all four permission
responses. No model or file write occurs. A separately scripted nonzero usage
update supplements the recorded zero cost to test cumulative-cost subtraction;
that synthetic amount is not a reported real inference charge.

## Codex JSONL (Step 12)

`codex-permissions.json` contains two actual Windows CLI 0.160.0 cases with
`gpt-5.6-luna` through the existing ChatGPT login (13 frames total). `permissions`
records the initial disabled Code Mode host error; it is intentionally replayed
as failure even though that old run eventually emitted `turn.completed`.
`permissions-final` records an allowed Work write, protected Agents write denied
with Windows access-denied output, and a successful synthetic out-of-scope read
(the explicitly confirmed broad-read fallback, **not** claimed confinement).
Vault prefixes in commands and nested command output are replaced with `C:/Vault`;
no auth/config metadata or secret values are included.

Tests replay the recorded frames in seven-byte fragments, including Unicode,
without inference or filesystem writes. Native token counts are cumulative per
Codex thread; there is no native dollar-cost field. See `step12-checks.json` for
the latest-per-thread usage audit, failed/repeated attempts, and paid Claude costs.
